channel.title: FixMyError.net – Recently Added Errors
channel.description: Newly added developer and infrastructure error fixes on FixMyError.net.

item.title: .NET: The framework 'Microsoft.NETCore.App', version '8.0.0' was not found
item.description: The published application is framework dependent and the machine has no matching runtime. Roll forward will pick a newer patch of the same major version but never a different major, so an app built for 8.0 will not start on a box that only has 9.0 installed.

item.title: Angular: NG0100: ExpressionChangedAfterItHasBeenCheckedError
item.description: A binding produced one value during change detection and a different one when Angular verified the pass in development mode. It normally means a parent reads state that a child mutates while initialising, so the check runs before the value has settled. Production builds skip the verification…

item.title: Apollo Client: Missing field 'x' while writing result to the cache
item.description: The normalised cache stores objects by id and typename, and the response left out a field the cache needed, usually because one query selects a subset that a fragment elsewhere expects. It is only a warning, but the later read returns incomplete data and refetches, which looks like a caching bug…

item.title: ASP.NET Core: Unable to resolve service for type while activating
item.description: The container was asked for a dependency nobody registered, so the controller or hosted service could not be constructed. The rest of the message names the type that needed it, which is the quickest way to tell whether the missing registration is yours or belongs to a library whose AddSomething…

item.title: AWS ECS: CannotPullContainerError, pull image manifest has been retried
item.description: The task could not fetch its image, and the reason is far more often networking than permissions: a task in a private subnet with no NAT gateway and no VPC endpoints cannot reach ECR at all. A task in a public subnet still needs assignPublicIp turned on before it has a route out.

item.title: AWS: The security token included in the request is expired
item.description: The temporary credentials issued by STS have passed their expiry, which is one hour by default for an assumed role. A long build, a laptop resumed from sleep with a stale cache, or a clock that has drifted by more than a few minutes all produce it even though credentials are clearly present.

item.title: bash: warning: setlocale: LC_ALL: cannot change locale
item.description: SSH forwards the client's locale variables and the server has no such locale generated, so every login prints the warning and programs fall back to the C locale. The fallback is the part that matters: sorting order, date parsing and Unicode handling all change underneath you.

item.title: Cargo: Blocking waiting for file lock on package cache
item.description: Cargo takes an exclusive lock on its home directory so two builds cannot corrupt the registry. The message is harmless while another build is genuinely running, but a lock left behind by a killed process, or a cache mounted read only in a container, makes the build wait for ever instead of failing.

item.title: Django: Forbidden (403) CSRF verification failed. Request aborted.
item.description: Django rejected the POST because the CSRF token or the request Origin did not match the session. Behind a reverse proxy the cause is usually not a missing token at all: since Django 4.0 the Origin header is compared against CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS, so a site served over HTTPS whose proxy forwards the…

item.title: Docker: image's platform (linux/amd64) does not match the detected host
item.description: The image has no build for the host architecture, so Docker Desktop runs it under emulation on Apple Silicon. It is a warning rather than an error, but emulated containers are slow and some binaries die with an illegal instruction, which is the failure people actually end up debugging.

item.title: docker: invalid reference format
item.description: Docker could not parse the image name. The usual causes are an uppercase letter in the repository part, a shell variable that expanded to nothing, or an unquoted path in a volume flag containing a space, which pushes the rest of the command into the position where the image name should be.

item.title: DOMException: play() failed because the user didn't interact with the document
item.description: Browsers block audible autoplay until the page has received a user gesture. play() returns a promise that rejects rather than throwing, so an unhandled rejection in the console is the only clue and the video simply sits there. Muted playback is still allowed, which is why the same code works on…

item.title: EF Core: another instance with the same key value is already being tracked
item.description: The change tracker already holds an entity with that primary key and Attach or Update tried to add a second copy. It normally follows a tracked read earlier in the request, then an update built from the request body. The first query is the cause even though the second call is what throws.

item.title: git: You have divergent branches and need to specify how to reconcile them
item.description: Local and remote have both moved on, and since Git 2.27 pull refuses to guess between merging and rebasing. The hint offers three settings without recommending one, which is why it is so often answered with a global config that then surprises everyone in the next repository.

item.title: git: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge
item.description: Git is protecting uncommitted work in files the incoming commits also touch, so nothing has been merged yet. When the listed files are ones you never edited, the cause is usually a line ending or file mode difference the working tree recorded on checkout rather than an edit of yours.

item.title: Go: module declares its path as X but was required as Y
item.description: The module line inside the dependency's go.mod does not match the import path you asked for. It shows up after a repository is renamed or forked, and after a v2 release that omitted the /v2 suffix, because Go treats the major version as part of the import path rather than as metadata.

item.title: Go: panic: send on closed channel
item.description: A goroutine wrote to a channel another goroutine had already closed. The convention is that the sender closes and the receiver never does, and with several producers no single one of them has a safe moment to close. The panic surfaces in a producer even though the bug belongs to whoever closed…

item.title: GraphQL: Cannot return null for non-nullable field
item.description: A resolver returned null where the schema promised a value. GraphQL then propagates the failure upward until it reaches a nullable field, so one missing value can blank out a whole branch of the response. The field that actually returned null is in the error path, not in the message text.

item.title: Java: error: invalid target release: 21
item.description: The build asked javac for a release the JDK on PATH cannot produce, which means the compiler running the build is older than the version the project targets. IDEs keep their own JDK setting, so the same project often compiles in the IDE and fails from the command line or in CI.

item.title: Java: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace
item.description: Metaspace holds class metadata rather than objects, so raising the heap changes nothing. It fills when an application keeps loading classes: repeated hot redeploys inside one JVM, a proxy or scripting library generating a class per request, or a classloader kept alive by a single stray reference.

item.title: Kubernetes: node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector
item.description: No node carries the labels the pod insists on, so the scheduler rejects every candidate. It turns up after an upgrade that replaced nodes with a different label set, and in multi zone clusters where a pod is pinned to the zone of a volume it can no longer be placed near.

item.title: Kubernetes: pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims
item.description: The scheduler will not place the pod because its claim has no volume yet. With WaitForFirstConsumer binding a moment of this is normal, so it only matters when it persists: then the storage class is missing, the provisioner is unhealthy, or the claim asks for an access mode the driver does not…

item.title: Laravel: 419 Page Expired
item.description: The CSRF token sent with the form did not match the session, and Laravel answers with 419 rather than 403. Most of the time the session was never stored at all: a session driver pointing at an unreachable Redis, a SESSION_DOMAIN that does not match the host, or a load balancer spreading requests…

item.title: macOS: cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified
item.description: Gatekeeper blocked something that carries the quarantine attribute and is not notarised. Anything a browser downloads gets that attribute, while the same file fetched with curl does not, which is why one copy of a binary runs and another refuses.

item.title: MySQL: Table 'db.Users' doesn't exist
item.description: On Linux, table names are case sensitive because they are filenames, while macOS and Windows are not. Code that writes Users against a schema that created users therefore works everywhere except production. lower_case_table_names is fixed when the data directory is initialised, so it cannot be…

item.title: PHP-FPM: server reached pm.max_children setting, consider raising it
item.description: Every worker in the pool is busy, so new requests sit in the listen backlog until Nginx gives up with a 502 or 504. Raising max_children only helps if there is memory to back it: the real cause is usually workers blocked on a slow query or an outbound HTTP call that has no timeout.

item.title: PHP: Fatal error: Call to a member function x() on null
item.description: A method was called on a variable holding null, which PHP 8 treats as a fatal Error rather than a warning. The null is nearly always the result of a lookup that found nothing: a find() with no row, an unloaded relation, or a dependency that was never injected because the container quietly fell…

item.title: PostgreSQL: could not resize shared memory segment, No space left on device
item.description: Postgres allocates workspace for parallel queries in /dev/shm, and containers default that mount to 64 MB. The disk is not full: the message is about the shared memory filesystem, which is why the same query runs happily on a host and fails inside Docker or Kubernetes.

item.title: Python: JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
item.description: What was handed to json.loads was not JSON at all, most often an empty body, an HTML error or login page, or a compressed payload nobody decoded. Line 1 column 1 means the very first character was already wrong, so the thing to inspect is the response, not the parsing code.

item.title: Python: SyntaxWarning: invalid escape sequence '\d'
item.description: A backslash inside an ordinary string starts an escape sequence, and \d is not one of them. Python 3.12 promoted this from a hidden DeprecationWarning to a SyntaxWarning that prints by default, which is why code that was quiet for years started complaining after an upgrade. It is scheduled to…

item.title: Python: TypeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable
item.description: json.dumps only understands the built in types, so a datetime, Decimal, UUID, set or dataclass stops it. The value is usually buried in a structure assembled somewhere else, which is why the traceback points at the dumps call rather than at the code that produced it.

item.title: Rails: ActionController::InvalidAuthenticityToken
item.description: The CSRF token in the request did not match the one in the session. Rails keeps the session in a cookie signed with secret_key_base, so a deploy that rotated the secret, servers that disagree about it, or a form page cached by a CDN all produce this for people who were part way through a session.

item.title: React: Rendered more hooks than during the previous render
item.description: A hook ran on this render that did not run on the last one, which happens when a hook sits after an early return or inside a condition or a loop. React matches hooks by call order, so the mismatch is reported on the render after the one that actually broke the rule.

item.title: Redis: LOADING Redis is loading the dataset in memory
item.description: The server is replaying its RDB or AOF file after a restart and refuses commands until it finishes. On a large dataset that takes minutes, and a replica that keeps falling back to a full resync will return it again and again, which reads as an outage rather than as a cold start.

item.title: Redis: WRONGTYPE Operation against a key holding the wrong kind of value
item.description: The key exists but holds a different type from the one the command expects, for instance GET against a hash. In practice it means two parts of the system disagree about the shape of a key, usually because a prefix is missing and two features have collided on the same name.

item.title: ReferenceError: window is not defined
item.description: The module ran on the server, where there is no DOM. Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit and Remix all execute components and everything they import during the build or on each request, so a library that touches window at import time fails long before a browser is involved.

item.title: Ruby: Your Ruby version is 3.3.5, but your Gemfile specified 3.2.2
item.description: Bundler compares the running interpreter with the ruby directive in the Gemfile and refuses to go further. A version manager that did not switch, a system Ruby picked up by cron or a deploy user, or a .ruby-version file updated without the Gemfile are the usual explanations.

item.title: Rust: error: linker `link.exe` not found
item.description: The default Windows toolchain is msvc, which uses Microsoft's linker rather than shipping one of its own. Rustup installs the compiler but not the Visual Studio build tools, so the failure arrives at the very end of the first build, after everything has already compiled.

item.title: Spring Boot: IllegalStateException: Failed to load ApplicationContext
item.description: A test could not build its context, and the message that matters is further down the caused by chain rather than on the first line. The usual reasons are a bean the test slice does not scan, a property that only exists in the production profile, and a mock that was removed while the test still…

item.title: ssh: Received disconnect: Too many authentication failures
item.description: The server closed the connection after the client offered more keys than MaxAuthTries allows. The agent presents every key it holds before reaching the one that would work, so a laptop with a dozen keys fails against a host that permits six attempts while a fresh machine connects first time.

item.title: Temporary failure in name resolution (EAI_AGAIN)
item.description: The resolver received no usable answer at all, rather than a negative one, so the problem is the path to the resolver rather than the record. An empty or wrong /etc/resolv.conf, a container that inherited a host only nameserver, and UDP 53 dropped by a firewall all look like this while everything…

item.title: TypeScript: Cannot find module './x.js' or its corresponding type declarations
item.description: With module set to node16 or nodenext, TypeScript resolves imports exactly as Node does at runtime, so a relative ESM import has to carry the .js extension even though the file on disk is .ts. The same code compiles under the bundler resolution, which is why this appears the day a project changes…

item.title: TypeScript: Cannot redeclare block-scoped variable 'name'
item.description: A file with no import or export is treated as a script, not a module, so its top level declarations land in the global scope and collide with the DOM library or with another file. The name in the message is usually something like name, event or status that already exists on window.

item.title: Vue: [Vue warn]: Failed to resolve component
item.description: Vue looked up a tag used in a template and found nothing registered under that name. With script setup an import is the registration, so the causes are a missing import, a name that does not match the file's PascalCase form, or a component registered on a different app instance from the one…

item.title: Windows: 'x' is not recognized as an internal or external command
item.description: cmd searched PATH and found nothing by that name. An already open terminal keeps the environment it started with, so a program installed a minute ago looks missing until a new shell is opened. The other frequent cause is a per user installation while the shell runs as a different account.

item.title: Windows: The process cannot access the file because it is being used
item.description: Windows takes mandatory file locks, so a handle held anywhere blocks a delete or rename that would simply succeed on Linux. The holder is often not the obvious application: an antivirus scanner, the search indexer or an Explorer preview pane can keep a handle open long enough to break a build's…

item.title: Xcode: Command PhaseScriptExecution failed with a nonzero exit code
item.description: A Run Script build phase exited non zero, and Xcode reports its own wrapper rather than the script's message, which is buried higher up the log. Scripts that work in a terminal fail here because the build environment has a trimmed PATH and never loads an interactive shell profile.

item.title: Android: INSTALL_FAILED_UPDATE_INCOMPATIBLE
item.description: An app with the same package name is already installed but signed with a different key. Android will not let one signing identity replace another, so a debug build cannot overwrite a release build or a Play Store install of the same app.

item.title: Anthropic API: 429 rate_limit_error (tokens per minute)
item.description: The organisation exceeded its input or output token budget for the minute, not its request count. Large prompts burn the token bucket long before the request bucket, so throttling concurrency without shrinking prompts often changes nothing.

item.title: Apache: AH00558: Could not reliably determine the server's FQDN
item.description: ServerName is not set, so Apache guessed from the system hostname. It is a warning and the server starts, but the guessed name is used in redirects and self referential URLs, which is how a redirect can send a browser to an internal hostname it cannot reach.

item.title: apt: Could not get lock /var/lib/dpkg/lock-frontend
item.description: Another process holds the package manager lock. On a freshly booted Ubuntu machine it is nearly always unattended-upgrades running in the background, which is why cloud-init scripts and CI jobs hit it in the first minutes of a VM's life.

item.title: asyncio: Task was destroyed but it is pending!
item.description: The event loop shut down while a task was still running, so its coroutine never got to finish or clean up. It usually means a task was created with create_task and nobody kept a reference or awaited it, and the garbage collector took it away mid flight.

item.title: AWS CloudFormation: Stack is in ROLLBACK_COMPLETE state and can not be updated
item.description: The stack's first create failed and rolled back. A stack in that state has no resources and cannot be updated, only deleted and created again. It is specific to the initial create: a failed update leaves UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE, which can be updated.

item.title: AWS Lambda: Internal server error, malformed Lambda proxy response
item.description: API Gateway received something it could not turn into an HTTP response. With proxy integration the function must return an object with a numeric statusCode and a string body: returning a plain object, or a body that is not stringified, produces a 502 with nothing useful in the client's response.

item.title: AWS S3: Access Denied on an object encrypted with KMS
item.description: The bucket policy allows the read but the caller has no permission on the KMS key, so S3 cannot decrypt the object for them. Two policies must agree: the IAM or bucket policy for s3:GetObject, and the key policy for kms:Decrypt.

item.title: AWS S3: PermanentRedirect, wrong regional endpoint
item.description: The request went to the wrong regional endpoint. S3 bucket names are global but buckets live in one region, and Signature Version 4 signs the region, so a client configured for the wrong one cannot simply be redirected.

item.title: AWS: ThrottlingException: Rate exceeded
item.description: You hit an AWS API request rate limit. The limits are per account, per region and per API, so a noisy deployment tool, an autoscaling loop or a monitoring agent polling DescribeInstances can throttle unrelated work that shares the account.

item.title: Azure: AuthorizationFailed, the client does not have authorization
item.description: Azure RBAC denied the operation at the scope you targeted. Role assignments are inherited downward from management group to subscription to resource group, so a role granted on the wrong scope, or a deny assignment from a policy, produces this even when the role name looks right.

item.title: bash: $'\r': command not found
item.description: The script has Windows line endings. Bash treats the carriage return as part of the last token on each line, so commands, variables and the shebang all acquire an invisible character, producing errors that make no sense against the visible source.

item.title: bash: fork: retry: Resource temporarily unavailable
item.description: The kernel refused to create another process because a limit was reached: the per user process count, the cgroup's pids.max, or the system wide thread maximum. The shell cannot even fork the command that would diagnose it, which is what makes it feel like the machine has locked up.
